facts.fact: The Adwave guide gives an example SMART objective of generating 30 qualified leads through the website within a month.
facts.quote: "Generate **30** qualified leads through our website this month."

facts.fact: The Adwave guide's example objective for a local HVAC company is to increase inbound phone calls from a new TV ad campaign by 20% over the next quarter.
facts.quote: "Increase inbound phone calls from our new TV ad campaign by **20%** over the next quarter."

facts.fact: The Adwave guide's example objective for an e-commerce store is to boost online sales from email marketing by 15% during the holiday season.
facts.quote: "Boost online sales from our email marketing efforts by **15%** during the holiday season."

facts.fact: The Adwave guide's example objective for a new gym is to sign up 50 new members from a local advertising push before the end of the year.
facts.quote: "Sign up **50** new members from our local advertising push before the end of the year."

facts.fact: The page gives the marketing ROI formula as (Revenue Generated - Marketing Cost) / Marketing Cost × 100.
facts.quote: (Revenue Generated - Marketing Cost) / Marketing Cost × 100

facts.fact: In the page's illustrative example, a business spending $20,000 on a campaign that brings in $100,000 in new revenue has an ROI of 400%.
facts.quote: Let's say a business spends **$20,000** on a campaign and it brings in **$100,000** in new revenue. The ROI is a very healthy **400%**.

facts.fact: The page says First-Touch Attribution gives 100% of the credit to the very first marketing channel a customer engaged with.
facts.quote: This model gives **100%** of the credit to the very first marketing channel a customer ever engaged with.

facts.fact: The page says Last-Touch Attribution gives 100% of the credit to the final touchpoint before conversion.
facts.quote: this model gives **100%** of the credit to the final touchpoint right before the conversion.

facts.fact: In the page's restaurant example, the restaurant set aside a $3,000 budget for its Adwave TV campaign, covering spot creation and local channel airtime.
facts.quote: They set aside a **$3,000** budget for their Adwave TV campaign.

facts.fact: In the page's restaurant example, 80 tables used the BRUNCHTV promo code over the following month.
facts.quote: Over the next month, **80** tables use the "BRUNCHTV" code.

facts.fact: In the page's restaurant example, the average brunch check is $150 per table.
facts.quote: The restaurant knows the average brunch check for a table is **$150**.

facts.fact: In the page's restaurant example, 80 tables at $150 per table produce $12,000 in revenue.
facts.quote: **80 tables x $150/table = $12,000** in revenue.

facts.fact: In the page's restaurant example, the calculated ROI on the $3,000 Adwave TV campaign is 300%.
The page states that in its restaurant example, the business generated $4 in return for every $1 invested in its Adwave campaign.
facts.quote: for every **$1** they invested in their Adwave campaign, they generated **$4** in return.

facts.fact: The page describes a UTM-tagged or promo-code example in which a restaurant offers the code SAVE15 on its Adwave TV commercial, so viewers can mention it when booking or ordering online.
facts.quote: They display a unique promo code, **"SAVE15,"** that viewers can mention when they call to book or use for online orders.

facts.fact: In the page's restaurant example, the Adwave TV ad offers a free appetizer to callers who mention the code BRUNCHTV when booking.
facts.quote: Mention the code 'BRUNCHTV' when you book to get a free appetizer.

facts.fact: The page defines Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) as an efficiency metric that measures gross revenue against only the ad spend, while ROI accounts for total cost.
facts.quote: ROAS, however, is an **efficiency** metric, measuring gross revenue against just the ad spend.

facts.fact: The page uses a hypothetical subscription service example in which the average customer stays for 36 months.
facts.quote: Think about a subscription service where the average customer stays for **36 months**.

facts.fact: The page states that a 5:1 ratio, equal to a 400% ROI, is a solid benchmark that many marketers aim for.
facts.quote: A **5:1 ratio**, which is a **400% ROI**, is a solid benchmark that many marketers aim for.

facts.fact: The page says returns from digital search ads can be seen in just a few days, while TV and broader brand-building channels build momentum over weeks and months.
facts.quote: You can see returns from digital search ads in just a few days.
